samples.text:
Today, only a few huge technology companies control most of what people do on the internet, such as searching for information, shopping and using social media. Some people worry about this, but in my opinion it is mostly a positive development for ordinary users.

The main reason is that these big companies can offer very good services, and many of them are free. For example, anyone can use a search engine, send emails or watch videos without paying any money. Because these companies are so rich, they can invest a lot in new technology and make their products fast and easy to use. A small company would not have enough money to do this.

Another advantage is that it is easier for people to communicate when everyone use the same platforms. My family live in different countries, but we can talk every day using one messaging app. Also, small businesses can sell their products all over the world through a big online marketplace, which was impossible in the past.

However, there are some disadvantages. When a few company have so much power, they can collect a huge amount of information about their users and use it for advertising. Some people feel that their privacy is not protected. In addition, it is difficult for new companies to compete with them, so there are less choices for customers.

In conclusion, although there are some problems with privacy and competition, I believe that this situation is generally positive, because big technology companies give people free, useful services and connect people around the world. However, governments should make laws to protect users' personal data.

samples.text:
A handful of enormous technology firms now dominate internet search, social networking, online shopping and cloud computing. Although these companies provide popular and often free services, I believe that such a concentration of power is a negative development.

It is true that their size has brought some benefits. Large firms can afford to invest heavily in research, and this has produced fast, reliable services that billions of people use every day. Because so many people use the same platforms, communication across borders has also become much easier.

However, the main problem is the lack of competition. When one company controls most of a market, it can buy up or copy smaller rivals, which makes it very hard for new businesses to succeed. Without competition, there is less pressure to improve products or to treat customers and suppliers fairly. For example, independent sellers who depend on a single online marketplace may have to accept whatever fees and rules the platform decides to impose.

A second concern is the amount of personal data these companies hold. By tracking what users search for, buy and watch, they build detailed profiles that are used to target advertising and to keep people online for longer. Most users have little idea how this information is used, and there is always the risk that it is leaked or misused. Moreover, because these platforms decide what news and opinions people see, they have considerable influence over public debate, which is worrying when so few companies are involved.

In conclusion, while the dominance of a few technology giants has given people convenient services, it reduces competition, threatens privacy and concentrates too much influence in too few hands. Overall, therefore, I regard it as a negative development that governments needs to regulate more strongly.
samples.why: Clear negative position · benefits conceded then main ideas extended with examples · logical progression · good range of topic vocabulary (concentration of power, target advertising) · mostly accurate, one agreement slip.

samples.text:
Much of what people do online, from searching for information to shopping and keeping in touch with friends, now passes through the systems of a very small number of technology corporations. While this concentration has delivered undeniable conveniences, I believe its long-term consequences make it a predominantly negative development.

The benefits should be acknowledged. The scale of these firms allows them to offer sophisticated services free of charge, funded by advertising, and to invest in infrastructure and research that smaller companies could never afford. Their platforms have also created shared spaces in which people across the globe can communicate with ease.

The first cause for concern, however, is economic. Dominant platforms act simultaneously as marketplaces and competitors within those marketplaces, giving them both the ability and the incentive to favour their own products. Promising start-ups are frequently acquired before they can pose a threat, and the businesses that depend on these platforms for customers have little choice but to accept the terms imposed on them. Over time, reduced competition tends to mean slower innovation and fewer alternatives for consumers.

The second concern relates to personal and political freedom. These companies accumulate unprecedented quantities of data about individuals' habits, relationships and beliefs, and their business models depend on exploiting that information. At the same time, the algorithms that determine which content users encounter shape public opinion in ways that are neither transparent nor accountable to voters. When such influence is held by a handful of private organisations, a single policy change or failure can affect billions of people at once.

In conclusion, the dominance of a few technology giants has made the internet more convenient, but at the cost of competition, privacy and democratic accountability. It is, on balance, a negative development, and one that calls for more robust regulation.
samples.why: Well-developed negative judgement · economic and political arguments fully extended and precisely supported · effective paragraphing and cohesion · wide, sophisticated vocabulary · wide range of structures with no noticeable errors.
